126: semisimple algebraic group $G$ and Borel subgroup $B$, has a classical
127: presentation due to Borel \cite{Borel}.  Pick a maximal torus
128: $T\subset B\subset G$, choose a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero, and let
129: $V=\Bbbk\otimes_{\ZZ} X(T)$, where $X(T)$ is the coweight lattice of
130: $T$.  Let $\Bbbk[V]:=\Sym(V^{\star})$ be the symmetric algebra for
131: $V^{\star}$; it naturally carries an action of the Weyl group $W :=
132: N_G(T)/T$.  Furthermore let $\Bbbk[V]^W$ be the ring of $W$-invariants
133: of $\Bbbk[V]$, and $\Bbbk[V]^W_+$ the ideal of $\Bbbk[V]$ generated by
134: the $W$-invariants of positive degree.  A classical theorem of Borel
135: \cite{Borel} states that
136: \begin{equation}
137: \label{Borel-presentation}
138: H^*(G/B,\Bbbk) \cong \Bbbk[V]/(\Bbbk[V]^W_+).
139: \end{equation}

claims.text: Assume \(A\) has Schur \(\mathbb Z\)-basis \(\{s_\mu:\mu\subseteq q^r\}\), is generated by \(h_1,\ldots,h_q\), and satisfies integral Pieri. Then \[ S=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu \] is an ideal of \(A\).

Under the additional Schur-span premise \[ J_v^{\mathbb Z}=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu \quad\text{inside }A, \] one has \(J_v^{\mathbb Z}=S\); after scalar extension, \(J_v=\Bbbk\otimes_{\mathbb Z}S\).

The supplied primary passages do not provide the needed identification between the Bruhat-span definition \(J_v=\Bbbk\text{-span}\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\) and the Schur span indexed by \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\). They also do not define an integral \(J_v^{\mathbb Z}\subseteq A\). Thus literal equality \(J_v=S\) is not source-grounded from the supplied material.
